reels.captionStart: الـ saturation بتاعتها طلعت 90% وهي بتتعب أكتر 👀
reels.question: Which investigation will most directly decide whether she needs ventilatory support?
reels.stem: A 66-year-old woman with COPD has had 2 days of worsening breathlessness. She is using her accessory muscles, her respiratory rate is 27 per minute, heart rate 104 per minute, and SpO2 87% on air. She is alert but tired. Oxygen through a Venturi mask has been started. Which investigation will most directly decide whether she needs ventilatory support?
reels.takeaway: In a hospitalised COPD exacerbation the arterial gas decides on ventilatory support, because only it shows PaCO2 and pH; oximetry, peak flow, and spirometry cannot detect hypercapnic acidosis.

reels.title: Case 02: episodes before breakfast, psychiatry referral
reels.question: What is the most appropriate next step?
reels.stem: A 44-year-old woman is referred to psychiatry with 6 months of episodes in which her husband finds her confused, sweating, and acting out of character, sometimes with double vision. Episodes happen before breakfast or after her morning run, once with a brief seizure, and each ends within minutes of a sweet drink. Between episodes her mental state is normal. She does not have diabetes, takes no medicines, and a CT head is normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
reels.answer: Measure plasma glucose during an episode
reels.takeaway: Episodic confusion, behaviour change, or seizures linked to fasting or exercise and relieved by carbohydrate suggest hypoglycaemia such as an insulinoma; measure glucose during an episode before making a psychiatric diagnosis.

reels.title: Case 04: tingling lips the day after thyroidectomy
reels.question: Which bedside finding would add the most specific support for hypocalcaemic tetany?
reels.captionStart: تنميل حوالين البُق تاني يوم بعد الـ thyroidectomy؟ ده hypocalcaemia بيسلّم عليك 🩺
reels.stem: A 40-year-old woman has perioral tingling on the day after total thyroidectomy. Calcium is 1.88 mmol/L (7.5 mg/dL). The examining student taps over the facial nerve in front of the ear and sees twitching of the upper lip. Her ECG shows a QTc of 490 ms. Which bedside finding would add the most specific support for hypocalcaemic tetany?
reels.answer: Carpal spasm after a cuff above systolic for 3 minutes
reels.takeaway: Trousseau sign is more specific for latent tetany than Chvostek sign, which is often positive in healthy people. After thyroidectomy, low PTH lets calcium fall; treatment is IV calcium gluconate with vitamin D.

reels.title: Case 04: respiratory depression on codeine with a high morphine level

reels.stem: A man taking codeine for pain develops respiratory depression, and his serum morphine level is high. Which genotype explains this?
reels.takeaway: CYP2D6 gene amplification makes a patient an ultra-rapid metaboliser, and codeine then raises serum morphine enough to cause respiratory depression. Pinpoint pupils with shallow breathing after an opioid point to opioid toxicity; naloxone reverses it.

reels.takeaway: Always assume testicular torsion in an acute scrotum until proven otherwise, and explore urgently if it cannot be excluded. reels.title: Case 08: potassium 6.9 with peaked T waves after a syncope
reels.question: Which treatment is given first to protect the heart from arrhythmias?
reels.captionStart: وقع في الغيط… والـ ECG بيقول hyperkalaemia ⚡
reels.stem: A 74-year-old man with chronic kidney disease is brought to the emergency department after a syncope. He is alert and has muscle weakness. His serum potassium is 6.9 mEq/L and the ECG shows peaked T waves. Which treatment is given first to protect the heart from arrhythmias?
reels.takeaway: Hyperkalaemia with ECG abnormalities is treated first with intravenous calcium gluconate for cardiac membrane stabilisation. Calcium gluconate antagonises the potassium effect on the heart and stabilises the cardiac membrane. The shift treatments and the methods that remove potassium come after it, with dialysis last.

reels.title: Case 09: painful eye and haloes after a dark cinema
reels.question: Which treatment brings immediate relief?
reels.captionStart: قوس قزح حوالين النور؟ ممكن يكون acute angle-closure glaucoma 👁️
reels.stem: A woman with a shallow anterior chamber develops a painful eye with misty vision and rainbow haloes after her pupil dilates in a dark room. The cornea is slightly opaque. Which treatment brings immediate relief?
reels.answer: A miotic drug such as pilocarpine
reels.takeaway: A miotic drug such as pilocarpine gives immediate relief in acute angle-closure glaucoma by constricting the pupil. The pupil constricts and pulls away from the filtration angle, which the base of the iris had blocked. A peripheral iridectomy may subsequently be performed to prevent further attacks.

reels.title: Case 10: sudden severe headache on sneezing with collapse
reels.question: Which imaging is best?
reels.stem: A woman aged 20 collapses after a sudden severe headache that began when she sneezed. She keeps covering her eyes because light bothers her and she has double vision. She is drowsy but fully conscious, and her blood pressure is 180/90. Which imaging is best?
reels.answer: CT brain and CT angiography head and neck
reels.takeaway: Subarachnoid haemorrhage is imaged with CT brain and CT angiography of the head and neck. Carotid duplex and echo are TIA investigations, not the imaging for a sudden severe headache with collapse.

reels.title: Case 11: shoulder dystocia, help already called
reels.question: Which manoeuvre should be performed first?
reels.stem: A shoulder dystocia is recognised in a woman in the second stage of labour. Additional help has been called. Which manoeuvre should be performed first?
reels.takeaway: Recognition of shoulder dystocia is followed at once by a call for additional help. The McRoberts' manoeuvre is the first manoeuvre for a shoulder dystocia; suprapubic pressure is applied with it as an adjunct. Fundal pressure is never used in shoulder dystocia because of neonatal harm and uterine rupture.

reels.title: Case 13: fever, headache, sore neck, and photophobia in the clinic

reels.title: Case 14: chest injury, distended neck veins, low pressure, and a silent left chest in the primary survey
reels.question: What is the most likely cause of his hypotension?
reels.captionStart: حادثة على الدائري؟ والـ primary survey هي اللي هتنقذه 🩺
reels.stem: A man with a normal airway is hypotensive after a chest injury. His neck veins are distended and there are no breath sounds on the left side. What is the most likely cause of his hypotension?
reels.answer: Tension pneumothorax, decompressed at once with a needle thoracocentesis (then a chest tube), with no X-ray first
reels.takeaway: Hypotension with distended neck veins and no breath sounds on one side is tension pneumothorax. It is a clinical diagnosis: decompress with a needle thoracocentesis during the primary survey, before moving on to C. Normal breath sounds with distended neck veins point to cardiac tamponade instead.
